task: 7. BLE radio tuning and runtime evidence
firmwareBuildReason: No BLE/FAP source or config files were modified in this task, so the required FAP build gate for firmware code changes was not applicable.
staticFindings: ATT MTU configured maximum is 414 bytes via CFG_BLE_MAX_ATT_MTU and stack init uses it; negotiated MTU is only knowable from ACI_ATT_EXCHANGE_MTU_RESP runtime logs.
DLE is enabled at stack init via CFG_BLE_DATA_LENGTH_EXTENSION=1, but product code has no explicit hci_le_set_data_length call and no captured runtime data-length-change values.
2M PHY is preferred with hci_le_set_default_phy(... TX_2M_PREFERRED, RX_2M_PREFERRED); product code has no explicit per-connection hci_le_set_phy tuning call.
AirBridge profile requests connection interval 0x0006..0x24 (7.5..45 ms), latency 0; actual accepted interval requires live connection logs.
AirBridge serial characteristic max is 244 bytes, ext update fragments are <=243 bytes, while bridge relay frames remain 64-byte HID-sized records carrying the browser protocol's 59-byte payload.
decision: No tuning/logging code change was justified without runtime evidence. The existing static parameters are already aggressive for throughput; runtime measurement is deferred until hardware is present.
preservedBehaviorScope: No web crypto/NACK protocol files modified.
No Bridge advertising watchdog or BLE disconnect behavior modified.
nextHardwareRunChecklist: Launch persistent Chrome with CDP at http://localhost:9222 and use it for any browser-gated QA.

Connect WebHID + Web Bluetooth with physical-gate protocol and capture serial/browser logs.
Record MTU, PHY, DLE/packet-size evidence, connection interval, bidirectional text, attachment SHA, throughput, cancel behavior, and Flipper DROP/TXERR counters.
